units: <cite ref="Tosefta Bekhorot 4:4">Tosef. Bekh. IV, 4</cite> <he>אם … דוֹמַעַת</he> if his eye is tearing.

<cite ref="Bekhorot 44a">Bekh. 44ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="D00850"><he>דָּלַף</he></cite>. [<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 157:11">Sifré Deut. 157</cite> <he>עד שיהו … דומעות</he>, read: <he>שזלגו עיניו דְּמָעוֹת</he>; v.

senses.gloss: (denom. of דֶּמַע II) to make a thing, otherwise exempt, subject to the law of T’rumah, to mix secular grain, wine, oil &c. with T’rumah in proportions sufficient to make the whole prohibited to non-priests; in gen. to mix secular with sacred things.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 2:4">Orl. II, 4</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 2:6">6</cite> <he>המְדַמֵּעַ</he>; a. fr.—
Ter. III, 1 אינה מְדַמַּעַת וכ׳ does not make Dema by itself (if mixed with secular fruits).
Ib. 2 אינה מְדַמֵּעֲתָן does not make them dema; מְדַמְּעוֹת כקטנה וכ׳ make dema, the smallest of the two being considered as an admixture; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְדוּמָּע.

<cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 5:6">Ib. V, 6</cite> <he>אין המדומע מדמע וכ׳</he> that which became subject to the law of T’rumah through an admixture, can affect a second mixture only in proportion, i.e. according to the quantity of real T’rumah contained therein.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chagigah 3:4">Ḥag. III, 4</cite> wine jars or oil jars <he>המְדוּמָּעוֹת</he> which have been mixed up; expl.
<cite ref="Chagigah 25b">ib. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>מד׳ דקדש</he> containing liquids, a portion of which was designated for libations.

senses.gloss: to become Dema through mixture. Ter. l. c.
units: <cite ref="Niddah 46b:52">Nidd. 46ᵇ</cite> <he>עיסה שנִדְמְעָה</he> if a sufficient quantity of T’rumah has been put in a dough to make it forbidden to non-priests; a. e.
